intro: A convolution reuses its kernel across spatial positions. Grouping controls channel connectivity while image size controls compute.
task: Count weight parameters, optional biases, and multiply-accumulates for one output image.
signature: convolution_budget(input_channels, output_channels, kernel, groups, output_size, bias)
requirements: Channel counts and groups are integers 1..64, with both channel counts divisible by groups. kernel and output_size are two-entry integer vectors in 1..64. bias is integer 0 or 1.

Return {"weights": scalar, "biases": scalar, "parameters": scalar, "macs": scalar}. weights=output_channels*(input_channels/groups)*kernel area; biases=bias*output_channels; macs=weights*output area, excluding bias additions.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Each grouped output sees only input_channels/groups input channels.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Output positions share parameters; multiply the operation count by area.

explanation: Sharing weights keeps parameter storage independent of image area. Computation still grows because each output position applies the same kernel.
Divisibility expresses valid grouping of channel connections. A depthwise layer uses one group per input channel, potentially with multiple outputs per group.
